author: R2
objection: Raw restricted gain is scale-dependent; maximizing alpha alone can amplify anatomical residual and cannot select lambda.
cited_evidence_or_counterexample: Uniform row scaling multiplies alpha, epsilon and rho by the same magnitude; scaling image rows changes both estimator and misspecification.
author_response: Accepted; fix output norm and observation metric, compare full error-to-gain ratio under same convention; no tuning by gain maximization.
modification: DOSSIERS/R2.md, Round 1 mathematical review response, R3-R1-1. Observed by direct read.

author: R2
objection: The local nonlinear inverse bound needs explicit candidate localization; low residual alone cannot imply membership in the truth-centered neighborhood.
cited_evidence_or_counterexample: F(t)=(cos t,sin t) has full local derivative yet repeated distant exact observations.
author_response: Accepted; requires ell_hat in S intersect B(ell*,R), connecting segment validity and kappa=sigma-LR/2>0 before error <=(2epsilon+rho)/kappa; initializer trust ball needs truth-in-ball premise.
modification: DOSSIERS/R2.md, Round 1 mathematical review response, R3-R1-2. Observed by direct read.

author: R2
objection: A hard graph admissible set can change discontinuously under a vanishing operator perturbation; fixed-S tauB cannot absorb it.
cited_evidence_or_counterexample: K_0=0, K_w=w[1,-1], w>0. Operator norm perturbation sqrt(2)w tends to zero but ker K_w requires p1=p2; target(.9,.1) remains distance sqrt(.32) from that set.
author_response: Accepted; tauB applies fixed S. Changing graph topology requires changed S, alpha, eta or another set-stability result. Add hard-vs-soft false-bridge analytic control.
modification: DOSSIERS/R2.md, Round 1 mathematical review response, R3-R1-3. Observed by direct read.
